title: Orrery model v1
description: An architecture model: components, the connections between them, the groups they sit in, what each component needs to stay healthy, plus views (drawings) and scenarios (what-ifs) over that model. Specification: docs/MODEL.md.

$schema.description: Schema URL, for editor validation and completion.

title.description: Title of the system. Shown on views that do not set their own.

direction.description: Default flow direction for views: connections run left-to-right ("right") or top-to-bottom ("down"). The only layout hint at this level; positions are computed automatically and are deterministic. Narrow, top-down diagrams read best on phones.

states.description: Your state vocabulary bound to how each state looks and behaves. Omit for the defaults: on (normal, rank 0), degraded (warn, 1), failed (alert, 2, unavailable, stops flow), off (muted, 2, unavailable, stops flow, cascades to children). Define an existing name to override it, a new name to extend, or set replace to start from nothing. The engine never reads a name; only look, rank, available, flows and cascade matter.

default.description: State of any entity that declares none, and what 'restore' returns to.

needs.description: Outcome states needs use unless they say otherwise.

unmet.description: State a component enters when fewer than 'min' alternatives of a need are available.

reduced.description: State a component enters when a need is met but not every alternative is available, or the preferred one is above the default rank.

replace.description: true: only the states in 'define' exist; 'default' and 'needs' must then name them.

oneOf.description: Preset: normal; warn (amber); alert (red, pulsing outline); muted (dimmed, dashed); highlight (blue glow).
Custom style. Only what you set changes; the rest stays normal.

pulse.description: Pulsing outline (animated; frame tooling freezes it).

rank.description: Severity order. Propagation only ever raises rank; the highest applies.

available.description: Whether an entity in this state counts toward a need's 'min'.

flows.description: 'stop': connections touching an entity in this state carry no flow.

cascade.description: 'children': every descendant of a group in this state is set to it as well.

description.description: What this state means to you. Shown in the legend; never read by the engine.

kinds.description: Your kind vocabulary for components and groups, bound to a glyph or a frame. Omit for the defaults. Kinds have no mechanics; they are words with a picture.

replace.description: true: only the kinds defined here exist.

glyph.description: A preset glyph name (service, database, queue, cache, gateway, client, storage, function, external) or SVG path data drawn in a 16×16 box.

description.description: What this kind means to you. Shown in the legend.

components.description: The running things: services, databases, queues, clients, external systems. A component is one deployment in one place; the same code in two regions is two components. Order matters: components that end up side by side keep this order, so list the important ones first.

id.description: Unique handle, shared id space with groups. Letters, digits, '_', '.', '-'; starts with a letter or digit.

label.description: Display name. Defaults to the id.

kind.description: What the component is, from 'kinds' (defaults: service, database, queue, cache, gateway, client, storage, function, external). Picks the glyph and box style; no mechanics. 'client' covers people and devices; 'external' is a system outside your control.

group.description: Id of the group this component sits in. Omit for top level.

state.description: Declared state in the base model, one of the names in 'states'. Defaults to states.default. Propagation only ever moves an entity to a higher-ranked state.

needs.description: What this component cannot work without. Each entry is either an entity id (component or group: a hard need with one way to satisfy it) or an object listing alternatives with the states to enter when the need is unmet or only partly met. Every alternative must be connected to this component (either direction) and must not be a group that contains it. Needs add no lines; they make existing lines matter and are drawn as a cue on them. AND across entries, OR within 'any'.

oneOf.description: An entity id: hard need, single alternative.

any.description: Alternative entities (components or groups) that satisfy this need, in order of preference. The first healthy one carries shifted load.

min.description: How many alternatives must be healthy for the need to be met (quorum). Must not exceed the number of alternatives.

unmet.description: State this component enters when fewer than 'min' alternatives are available. Defaults to states.needs.unmet (failed). A nice-to-have call is "unmet": "degraded".

reduced.description: State this component enters when the need is met with reduced redundancy. Defaults to states.needs.reduced (degraded).

replicas.description: How many instances run. Drawn as a stacked box with the count. No health semantics in v1.

description.description: One or two sentences. Shown as a tooltip and in the outline.

meta.description: Free-form data ignored by rendering and semantics: owner, url, tags, cost centre. The only place unknown keys are allowed.

connections.description: What one entity does to another: calls it, publishes to it, replicates to it, streams data to it. Either end may be a component or a group (even an empty one). Directed from the initiator ('from') to the target ('to'). Connections carry no health semantics; see 'needs' for that. Two connections between the same pair must both have ids.

from.description: Initiating entity id: a component or a group.

to.description: Target entity id: a component or a group. The arrowhead is drawn here; on a group it attaches to the frame.

id.description: Optional handle. Required when the same pair of components has more than one connection, so scenarios can tell them apart.

kind.description: How it is drawn: sync solid, async dashed, replication dotted, dataflow thick. No health semantics.

label.description: Short text on the line: protocol or purpose.

load.description: Relative traffic, 0 to 1: speed and weight of the animated flow. 0 hides the flow. Relative intensity, not real units. Shifts automatically when a need's alternative goes down.

bidirectional.description: Draw arrowheads at both ends. The flow still animates from 'from' to 'to'.

meta.description: Free-form data ignored by rendering and semantics: owner, url, tags, cost centre. The only place unknown keys are allowed.

groups.description: Containers drawn as labelled frames: tiers, regions, zones, clusters, trust boundaries, or whole systems not opened yet. May be empty (a black box). Nest with 'parent'. Groups can be connected, needed and failed like components. The hierarchy is also the outline for navigation.

id.description: Unique handle, shared id space with components.

label.description: Frame title. Defaults to the id.

kind.description: What the container represents, from 'kinds' (defaults: tier, region, zone, cluster, boundary). Picks the frame style; no mechanics.

parent.description: Id of the enclosing group. Omit for top level. Cycles are rejected.

meta.description: Free-form data ignored by rendering and semantics: owner, url, tags, cost centre. The only place unknown keys are allowed.

state.description: Declared state of the group as an entity: what connections and needs pointing at the group see. Defaults to states.default. Reaches members only if the state cascades. A non-empty group is also derived from its members through the ordinary need mechanic.

description.description: One or two sentences. Shown as a tooltip and in the outline.

views.description: Drawings of the model. Optional: without it, one topology view of everything is rendered. Pick one with `orrery render --view <id>`. Connections with one end outside a view are drawn to a ghost of the outside component, never dropped.

title.description: Title for this view. Defaults to the document title.

type.description: Kind of drawing. Only 'topology' exists today; 'sequence' and 'walkthrough' are reserved.

direction.description: Flow direction for this view. Defaults to the document direction.

scope.description: Group id to drill into: that group becomes the outer frame and only its descendants are shown.

only.description: Show only these entities (a group id means the group and everything in it) plus the groups containing them. Combines with 'scope' by intersection.

scenarios.description: Named what-if stories. Each step sets declared states ('set'), restores them, or overrides a connection's load; steps are cumulative (step k applies steps 1..k). Propagation fills in every consequence. Render one with `orrery render --scenario <id> --step <n>`; try one-offs with `orrery render --set <state>=<id>`.

label.description: Human title. Defaults to the id.

steps.description: Ordered changes. A step must change at least one thing and may name an entity only once across 'set' and 'restore'.

note.description: What happens in this step, shown during step-through.

set.description: State name to entity id(s): "set": { "failed": "db", "off": ["eu-west"] }. Any name from 'states'. On a group, the state applies to the group as an entity and reaches its members only if the state cascades.

restore.description: Entity id(s) returned to their base-model state.

load.description: Connection load overrides. Refer to a connection by its ends, or by 'id' when the pair has several connections. Rarely needed: load shifts automatically when an alternative goes down.

from.description: Initiating entity id (with 'to'); a component or a group.

to.description: Target entity id (with 'from'); a component or a group.
